alignments.note: Conjunction waw → *And* (rule 14).
Construct noun with a supplied *the*, no article morpheme being present in the chain (rule 29).
Nomen rectum takes the *of* relation (rule 19); its *the* is supplied, no article morpheme standing on it (rule 29).
Inner nomen rectum with its *of* (rule 19).
Niphal verb rendered *was gone up*; headed on the lexical predicate (rule 24).

The compound preposition מֵעַל is rendered by the single English *from*, so the two morphemes share one unit under rule 30, headed on מִן, which carries the lexeme. The competing reading takes *from* as מִן's alone and marks עַל unrepresented under rule 2, on the ground that the *upon* sense is lost; I took the fusion because מֵעַל is one compound preposition of which no morpheme owns a part of the English.
Article → *the* (rule 15).
Noun *cherub*.

The relative, its preposition and the resumptive suffix are fused into the single English *whereupon* (rule 30), headed on the relative, which carries the *where-*. Splitting is impossible: one English token bears all three senses.
הָיָה with its English subject pronoun (rule 17), headed on the verb.
Preposition אֶל → *to*.

Construct noun with a supplied *the*: the ASV writes a *the* before both *threshold* and *house*, so the article morpheme takes the one before its own word and the construct takes the supplied one (rule 29).
Article takes the *the* standing before its own word (rule 29).
Nomen rectum with its *of* (rule 19).
Waw of the consecutive form → *and* (rule 14).
Verb with its subject pronoun (rule 17).
Preposition אֶל → *to*.
Article on אִישׁ takes the phrase's single *the* (rules 15, 47).
Noun *man*.
The attributive's agreement article is unrendered: the ASV writes no second *the* and no relative for *the man clothed in linen*, so the noun's article took the single determiner (rules 41, 47).
Passive participle → *clothed*.
The ASV writes no *the* for *in linen* (rule 29).
Accusative of material; the supplied *in* belongs to the noun licensing it (rule 33).
Relative אֲשֶׁר → *who*.
Construct noun → *inkhorn*.
The chain's single written *the* goes to the present article morpheme, English fronting it before the attributive *writer's* (rules 28, 29).
Nomen rectum rendered attributively → *writer's* (rule 28).

The verbless clause has a prepositional predicate, and the ASV recasts it possessively as *had ... by his side*: the supplied verb of that recasting joins the preposition heading the predicate (rules 43, 49), the unit being discontinuous around the object under rule 25 and headed on the preposition's own *by*. The competing readings put *had* on אֲשֶׁר as the possessive relative, or mark it added under rule 20's supplied-lexical-verb clause; I took the preposition because dropping *had* leaves only the possession relation diminished, which is rule 43's test.
מָתְנַיִם → *side*; the margin's *upon his loins* is the literal gloss only.
3ms suffix → *his* (rule 18).

review_notes: s010/s012/s013 are fused on *whereupon* under rule 30; the alternative would strand two morphemes as unrepresented beside a single rendered one, which that rule forbids.
s031 carries the recast possessive *had* under rules 43 and 49; the same construction recurs at EZK.9.11 and is read the same way there, though each verse was decided on its own evidence.
